t.2.78.1: Then, as soon as he saw the army encamped along the river Gaṅgā, the king of the Niṣādas hastily spoke to his kinsmen.
t.2.78.2: This mighty army, vast as the ocean, is seen over there; even pondering it in my mind, I cannot make out its end.
t.2.78.4: Now Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, is coming to slay Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, who has been banished from the kingdom by his father.
t.2.78.3: For this one here, of mighty frame, with the kovidāra banner on his chariot, will either have the fishermen bound or else he will slay us.
t.2.78.5: Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is both my master and my friend. Desiring his welfare, stand here armed and ready on the marshy bank of the Gaṅgā.
t.2.78.6: Let all the fishermen too take their stand along the river Gaṅgā, as guards of the river, endowed with strength and living on meat, roots and fruits.
t.2.78.7: "Let five hundred boats stand ready, each with a hundred young fishermen armed for battle," so he commanded.
t.2.78.8: When Bharata here proves to be well-disposed toward Rāma, then this army, attended by safety, will cross the Gaṅgā today.
t.2.78.9: Having spoken thus, Guha, lord of the Niṣādas, took a gift along with fish, meat and honey, and approached Bharata.
t.2.78.10: Seeing him approaching, the mighty son of the charioteer, versed in proper conduct, then reported it to Bharata in a humble manner.
t.2.78.11: This chieftain, surrounded by a thousand of his kinsmen, is well acquainted with the Daṇḍaka forest; he is old, and he is a friend of your brother.
t.2.78.12: Therefore, O Kākutstha, let Guha, the lord of the Niṣādas, see you; he knows without doubt where those two, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, are.
t.2.78.13: Having heard these auspicious words from Sumantra, Bharata quickly spoke, saying, "Let Guha see me."
t.2.78.14: Having obtained permission, Guha, delighted and surrounded by his kinsmen, approached Bharata and, bowing low, spoke these words.
t.2.78.16: There are roots and fruits gathered by the Niṣādas, and meat both fresh and dried, and a great abundance of forest fare of every kind.
t.2.78.15: This land is but a pleasure grove, and we have been taken unawares. We all place ourselves at your service; stay here in the home of your own Dāśa clan.
t.2.78.17: I trust your army, well fed, will stay here this night; honored with all manner of pleasures, you will set out tomorrow with your troops.
